h1: Santisook Midtown Pattani — a new riverside boutique rewriting where to stay in Pattani city
intro: If you came to Pattani years ago and grumbled that good-looking design stays in the city were hard to find, take a look at Santisook Midtown Pattani. This newly opened 3-star boutique sits right by Dechanuchit Bridge on the Pattani River, an easy walk to the old town and markets. It has just 20 rooms, but they are modern and stylish, with an in-house Rama Bistro cafe, halal breakfast and free parking. Standard rooms start from around ฿1,700/night.

body.html: Santisook Midtown is a newly opened hotel that many guests describe in their reviews as a pleasant surprise for Pattani city. The building stands on the Pattani River beside Dechanuchit Bridge, in the Anoru area, which is the old town at the heart of the city. From the front door it is just a few minutes' walk to markets, restaurants and Lim Ko Niao Shrine — a location made for people who would rather explore the city on foot than drive everywhere.

What sets it apart from the city's older hotels is a design that feels modern yet still warm. There are only 20 rooms, ranging from the 29 sqm Standard Twin up to the 58 sqm Suite and Family Suite. Some are Superior rooms with river views looking out over the water and the bridge. Guests often note that the rooms feel more spacious than expected for a city hotel, with comfortable beds and a Smart TV in every room.

"The room was sparkling clean and beautifully done — modern but easy to relax in. Staff looked after us so well, the breakfast was delicious, and you can walk to the markets and food. Incredible value for Pattani."

Breakfast is another point that earns regular praise. It is served à la carte with both local and international dishes, includes halal options, and the coffee comes from the in-house Rama Bistro cafe, which guests rate highly. Sipping coffee by the river in the morning before heading out is an atmosphere you rarely get from other stays in the city. Friendly, helpful staff are something almost every review mentions.

On facilities, the hotel offers free private parking, free Wi-Fi in rooms and public areas, luggage storage and a small meeting room. There is car rental and a place to leave your bags if you arrive early or leave late. The central location means you can head out to eat, browse the markets or visit the shrine without relying much on a car — a real contrast to the hotels out in the Rusamilae area, which require a drive into town.

To be honest, the limits here come from being a small hotel. Parking is limited, so at busy times a space can be a little tricky to find, and with only 20 rooms it books up fast on weekends and holidays. There is no pool or gym like a larger hotel, so if you want a full set of facilities you will need to look elsewhere. And because it sits in the heart of the old town, some nights you may hear a little street noise, though most guests say the rooms insulate sound well.

With a high 9.8 score from 208 reviews on Trip.com and consistently warm feedback, Santisook Midtown has become one of the first names that comes up for travellers wanting a clean, well-designed stay in central Pattani at a price that stays reasonable. If your trip is about wandering the old town, sampling local food and basing yourself somewhere that feels new and easy on the eye, this is a place that fits.

honestSummary: Santisook Midtown is the best new boutique for anyone wanting a stylish stay in central Pattani — new, clean rooms, a riverside location within walking distance of everything, and a cafe and breakfast that win plenty of praise. The trade-off is a small hotel with limited parking and no pool, but if your trip is about exploring the old town on foot, it fits beautifully.
honestChecks: If you're driving in with a big group and need plenty of parking — parking here is limited and you may have to park further away at busy times → the Rusamilae-area hotels have more space.
If you want a swimming pool or a gym — this small boutique has neither → look at a larger city hotel with a pool instead.
If you're here to walk the old town, eat local food and want somewhere new and clean — the riverside, central location puts everything within walking distance → this is the best fit in Pattani.

tips.body: Some rooms look out over the Pattani River and Dechanuchit Bridge. Request a river view when you book — the morning light is the prettiest.

tips.title: Explore the Anoru old town on foot
tips.body: The central location puts Lim Ko Niao Shrine, the markets and the old-town buildings of Anoru within easy walking distance — no car needed.

faq.q: Where is Santisook Midtown and what's nearby?
faq.a: Santisook Midtown is at 5 Phiphit Road, Anoru, Mueang Pattani, right beside Dechanuchit Bridge on the Pattani River in the city centre. It's about a 12-minute walk to Lim Ko Niao Shrine, with markets and old-town restaurants within walking distance. Prince of Songkla University, Pattani is about a 12-minute drive.

faq.q: How much does Santisook Midtown cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Standard rooms start from around ฿1,700/night. Options run from the Standard Twin (29 sqm) and the river-view Superior Double up to the Suite and Family Suite (58 sqm), at roughly ฿2,400–฿2,900. Prices vary by date and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Does Santisook Midtown have breakfast and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both. Breakfast is served à la carte from 07:00–10:00 with local and international dishes and halal options. Free private parking is available, though space is limited, so at busy times you may have to park a little further away.

faq.q: Who is Santisook Midtown best for?
faq.a: It suits couples, travellers who want to explore the old town on foot, and anyone wanting a new, clean, well-designed stay in central Pattani. The riverside location is within walking distance of the markets and shrine. If you need a pool or lots of parking, a larger hotel in the Rusamilae area may suit better.

faq.q: Does Santisook Midtown have river-view rooms?
faq.a: Yes. Some Superior Double rooms look out over the Pattani River and Dechanuchit Bridge. Request a river view when you book — the morning light by the water is the prettiest time, ideal for a coffee before heading out.
